details.description: Alias for TypeSafe's newest stable Jev release (jev-1.14.0 on 2026-11-08); it moves when TypeSafe ships a new release, and responses name the pinned version. Jev is TypeSafe's flagship System One model: it answers typed questions about the input with calibrated probabilities instead of generated text.
advantages: Answers typed questions (Noul, Choice, Score) with probabilities that code can branch on directly, instead of generated text.
Trained for calibrated decisions; answers can carry a confidence for deciding when to act on its own and when to ask for review.
No fixed cap on the number of questions per request, as long as the 64K per-request and 32K per-question context limits are met.
Billed on input tokens only; output tokens are free.
disadvantages: Moves to a new model when TypeSafe ships a release; use jev-1.14.0 to pin the version.
Does not write replies, produce code or explain its reasoning.
Calibration is measured across groups of predictions; it does not guarantee that an individual answer is correct.
64K tokens per request and 32K per question; TypeSafe's opt-in 262K long-context mode is not used by Bud.
TypeSafe accepts PNG and JPEG images, but Bud's System One adapter sends text only in this release.
Box questions (bounding boxes over images) are not available through Bud.
use_cases: Routing support tickets to the right team
Detecting refund requests and other intents in customer messages
Gating automated actions on a confidence threshold, with human review for uncertain cases
Combining several independent checks with deterministic rules in code

details.description: Laya is Embedding Space's open-source System 1 decision model, served through Embedding Studio's decide API. It returns a typed answer from a fixed set with a calibrated confidence and a conformal prediction set, abstains when no single option reaches the calibrated bar, and routes uncertain records to human review.
advantages: Confidence is calibrated rather than taken from a softmax, with abstention when no single option clears the bar.
Projects can be fitted on your own labels, measured and replayed; the trained policy can be downloaded and served locally with laya, giving the same answers as the hosted API.
The engine is open source.
Priced per decision rather than per token.
Embedding Space reports a 33 ms median per decision.
disadvantages: No token usage is reported; Bud bills a fixed price per request.
Choice questions are capped at 128 options in Bud: 255 failed live with an out-of-memory error (2026-11-08).
Abstention, the review route and the conformal set are not returned through Bud's Decisions API; Bud returns probabilities and confidence.
Embedding Studio also accepts images, audio and video, but Bud sends text only.
use_cases: Agent guard rails and agent action gating
Support ticket routing and email triage
Document sorting, lead qualification and product review triage
